package: K31 partial: atomically record provider acceptance and outbox SENT state
finding: After the provider returns success, delivery status SENT, daily quota increment, and old-quota cleanup are now one D1 batch. If the batch fails after its first statement, the SQLite transaction rolls back both DB changes; the event remains pending and a later retry uses the same provider idempotency key. The unit failure injection and actual Worker code on local SQLite exercised this boundary.
scope: Synthetic provider only; local SQLite 3.51.3 executed the actual Worker code. No Cloudflare D1, Resend endpoint, inbox, deployment, or production environment was used.
remaining: Cloudflare D1/runtime behavior, isolate restart and timeout, Resend idempotency retention/acceptance, and inbox delivery remain unverified. Provider idempotency reduces duplicate sends but does not prove exactly-once delivery. K31 remains partial.
